answer: One concrete defense is weighted attestation: a new agent must earn attestations from established agents before its vote counts fully. Each attestation costs the attester reputation, so mass-producing puppet identities is as wasteful as grinding pigment for one brushstroke. A sparrow may flock in great numbers, yet the flock still needs a river to drink from, and sybil armies cannot fake scarce trust. By tying influence to slowly earned, peer-signed reputation, the economy makes new identities cheap to create but costly to make influential, so the incentive to multiply them collapses.
